articles.title: Indian finance influencer with over 1 million followers found dead amid cyberbullying allegations
articles.text:
A 27-year-old Indian financial influencer with more than one million social media followers has been found dead near Chennai, with police investigating allegations that he was subjected to sustained online harassment. V Harish, a financial consultant from Puducherry who operated under the name “Finance with Harish,” was found dead at a rented villa near Muttukadu on Monday night (October 19). According to Indian media reports, police are investigating his death as a suspected suicide following a complaint filed by his father, J Vinayagam. Harish had built a large online following over five years by sharing content related to finance and investments. However, his social media accounts were reportedly blocked in September following complaints about his financial advice and professional credentials. His father alleged that another social media influencer, Jason Samuel, had subjected Harish to cyberbullying, defamatory accusations and threats, causing him severe mental distress. According to the complaint, Harish recorded a video before his death in which he allegedly blamed Samuel for his decision. Samuel has denied the allegations, saying he had raised legitimate questions about Harish’s qualifications and whether he was authorised to provide financial advice. He alleged that Harish did not possess the required registration from India’s Securities and Exchange Board and had misrepresented his professional credentials. Samuel also said he had never expected Harish to die by suicide. Police said Harish’s established social media accounts had been blocked following mass reporting, while a replacement account was also subsequently taken down. Investigators are examining the allegations made by both parties, including the circumstances surrounding the removal of his accounts and the video reportedly recorded before his death. No suicide note was recovered, and police have registered a case of unnatural death. The allegations against Samuel have not been independently established, and the investigation remains ongoing. articles.title: How a Rs. 100 payment triggered a bribery arrest at a bus stand
articles.text:
An officer attached to the Gampaha Regional Office of the Road Passenger Transport Authority has been arrested for allegedly soliciting and accepting a bribe of Rs. 100.
According to the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC), the officer allegedly demanded the money to allow a bus operating on Route 188 from Raddolugama to Colombo to depart later than its scheduled time and provide the bus crew with a favourable departure arrangement.
The suspect, identified as a timetable officer, was arrested by CIABOC investigators at approximately 12:25 p.m. on October 20 inside the timetable office at the Raddolugama bus stand.
The arrest was made following a complaint lodged by a person working on the bus.

articles.title: Myanmar national arrested with Rs. 46 Mn worth of Kush at BIA
articles.text:
A 22-year-old Myanmar national has been arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake for allegedly attempting to smuggle a consignment of Kush drugs worth over Rs. 46 million into Sri Lanka.
The suspect was arrested by officers of the Airport Police Narcotics Bureau in the early hours of today (21), while attempting to leave the airport.
According to reports, the suspect had arrived at the BIA at around 1.45 a.m. aboard Thai Airways flight TG-307 from Bangkok, Thailand.
During an inspection of his luggage, officers discovered 4.646 kilograms of Kush drugs, valued at Rs. 46.46 million, concealed in three parcels among clothes, sweets and food items.
The suspect, along with the seized drugs, is scheduled to be produced before the Negombo Magistrate’s Court today.
He is thereafter expected to be handed over to the Police Narcotics Bureau headquarters in Colombo for further questioning and investigations.

articles.title: Expert Committee discusses investigation into Tusker Kawanthissa’s death
articles.text:
The expert committee appointed by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to investigate the death of Sri Lankan tusker Kawanthissa held its first meeting at the Presidential Secretariat today (21).
According to the President’s Media Division (PMD), the meeting was held under the patronage of Presidential Chief of Staff Prabath Chandrakeerthi.
The committee was appointed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of Kawanthissa, who died on or around October 16, 2026, in the Siyambalangamuwa area of Galgamuwa.
The committee has also been tasked with developing a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the welfare of wild elephants and submitting recommendations for a national elephant conservation programme.
During the meeting, discussions focused on the cause of Kawanthissa’s death, the nature of the injuries sustained by the tusker and the involvement of the Department of Wildlife Conservation.
The committee also discussed developing scientifically based procedures to ensure prompt action in similar incidents in the future.
According to the PMD, discussions were held on establishing a Rapid Response Veterinary Unit to provide immediate veterinary assistance to wild elephants in the field.
It was also decided to seek the assistance of local and international experts in developing the proposed conservation measures.
The meeting was attended by Expert Committee Chairman A. H. Sarath Wijesinghe, Committee Coordinator W. W. Harrison and other members, including academics, wildlife experts and legal professionals.
articles.summary: The expert committee appointed by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to investigate the death of Sri Lankan tusker Kawanthissa held its first meeting at the Presidential Secretariat today (21). During the meeting, discussions focused on the cause of Kawanthissa’s death, the nature of the injuries sustained by the tusker and the involvement of the Department of Wildlife Conservation.

articles.title: New liquor outlets in Jaffna and Kilinochchi: Shanakiyan questions Govt
articles.text:
ITAK Parliamentary Group Leader MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam has strongly opposed the establishment of additional liquor outlets in Jaffna and Kilinochchi, urging the government to prioritise development and public welfare in the Northern Province.
Raising questions in Parliament today (21) under Standing Order 27(2), the MP expressed concerns over proposals to open new liquor outlets in the two districts, citing public objections and the proposed locations near schools, temples and residential areas.
He stressed that development in the Northern Province should focus on improving livelihoods, public services and economic opportunities rather than increasing the number of liquor outlets.
MP Rasamanickam also questioned the government over the 361 liquor licences reportedly issued during former President Ranil Wickremesinghe’s administration in 2024.
He called for the disclosure of the names of politicians who had recommended the licences, details of the beneficiaries, findings of investigations into alleged irregularities and the number of licences subsequently cancelled.
The MP further raised concerns over the widespread production and sale of illicit alcohol, particularly in Batticaloa, calling for stricter enforcement and tougher penalties against repeat offenders.
He also questioned whether high taxes on legally produced alcohol were encouraging consumers to turn to cheaper illicit alternatives, potentially increasing alcohol-related health risks and the burden on the public healthcare system.
MP Rasamanickam requested district-wise statistics on illicit alcohol offences and repeat offenders for 2025 and 2026, along with details of liquor licences proposed, approved or issued in Jaffna and Kilinochchi since September 2024.
He urged the government to ensure transparency in liquor licensing, consider public objections and strengthen measures to combat illicit alcohol production and sales.
Responding to MP Shanakiyan’s questions, Deputy Minister of Economic Development Nishantha Jayaweera said that drafts have already been prepared to amend the Excise Ordinance to increase the penalties for offenders and the relevant process has already begun.
Deputy Minister Nishantha Jayaweera further said that the existing Ordinance has now been amended and that legal amendments will be incorporated into it in the future.
Stating that the shortcomings in the existing Ordinance have been identified and corrected, he added that it is expected to be approved soon.
articles.summary: ITAK Parliamentary Group Leader MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam has strongly opposed the establishment of additional liquor outlets in Jaffna and Kilinochchi, urging the government to prioritise development and public welfare in the Northern Province.

articles.title: Dutch PM Rob Jetten and partner expecting child via surrogate mother
articles.text:
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his partner, Argentine field hockey player Nicolás Keenan, are expecting their first child, the couple announced on Monday.
“Someone very special is on the way. See you in 2027, little one,” they wrote in a post on Instagram.
“There are no words big enough to thank our eggdonor, our surrogate mum Lisa and both their families. None of this would be possible without you,” they added.
Jetten’s party, D66, has also released a statement, saying the pregnancy was made possible thanks to a couple they are friends with who already have children of their own.
“The surrogate mother is Dutch, as is the egg donor,” the statement continued.
“This is not a case of commercial surrogacy. The surrogate mother and the egg donor are acquaintances of Jetten and Keenan. They are delighted to be able to help fulfil the two fathers-to-be’s dream of having a child in this way.”
Jetten and Keenan announced their engagement in November 2024.
“Being a surrogate mother feels like a very special way to help make our dear friends’ dream come true,” Lisa, the surrogate mother, was also quoted as saying.
Jetten was born in Veghel in the southern Netherlands in 1987 and grew up in nearby Uden. He went on to study at the Nijmegen School of Management before beginning his career at ProRail, which is responsible for maintaining railway infrastructure in the Netherlands.
He became a Member of the House of Representatives for D66 in 2017 and later worked as the minister for climate and energy policy under former Dutch PM Mark Rutte, who is now NATO secretary general. (Euronews)
articles.summary: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his partner, Argentine field hockey player Nicolás Keenan, are expecting their first child, the couple announced on Monday. The surrogate mother and the egg donor are acquaintances of Jetten and Keenan.

articles.title: Welimada supermarket fined Rs. 500,000 for selling rice above controlled price
articles.text:
A supermarket in Welimada has been fined Rs. 500,000 for selling imported Keeri Samba rice above the government-regulated maximum retail price (MRP).
The fine was imposed following a case filed by the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) against the supermarket for selling a kilogram of imported Keeri Samba rice at Rs. 260, exceeding the controlled price of Rs. 255 by Rs. 5.
According to the CAA, the violation was detected during an inspection conducted by officers of the CAA’s Badulla District Office on December 4, 2025.
During the inspection, a CAA investigating officer purchased one kilogram of imported Keeri Samba (GR 11) rice for Rs. 260, confirming that the supermarket had charged Rs. 5 above the stipulated maximum retail price.
The CAA continues to conduct raids and inspections across the country to ensure compliance with regulated prices of essential commodities and protect consumer rights.
The public has been urged to report incidents of overcharging and other violations of consumer protection laws through the CAA hotline 1977.

articles.title: India proposes ban on added sugars in baby food for infants
articles.text:
India’s food safety regulator has proposed banning the addition of certain sugars to baby food products intended for infants up to six months old, as part of efforts to improve child nutrition and protect infant health.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has published draft regulations seeking to prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose to infant nutrition products.
The proposed amendment, published in the Gazette of India on October 16, aims to reduce unnecessary exposure to added sugars during the critical early stages of childhood development.
Under existing regulations, manufacturers are permitted to add limited quantities of sucrose and fructose when necessary as carbohydrate sources. However, the proposed changes would completely prohibit their addition to products intended for babies up to six months old.
India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said the move is intended to ensure that infant food products meet appropriate nutritional standards while addressing health concerns associated with early sugar consumption, including childhood obesity and related health risks.
The ministry said the initiative also supports public health recommendations encouraging exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months of life.
The draft regulations have been opened for public consultation, with stakeholders given 60 days to submit objections and suggestions.
The proposed ban will take effect only after the regulations are finalised and brought into force.
articles.summary: India’s food safety regulator has proposed banning the addition of certain sugars to baby food products intended for infants up to six months old, as part of efforts to improve child nutrition and protect infant health. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has published draft regulations seeking to prohibit the addition of sucrose and fructose to infant nutrition products.

articles.title: Rs. 50 mn for Rumesh? Sajith cites reward scheme, Minister says circular outdated
articles.text:
Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa questioned Sports Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage in Parliament over the delay in paying Rs. 50 million to Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesha Tharanga in recognition of his international achievements.
Premadasa said the athlete had brought significant recognition to Sri Lanka through his performances at international competitions and questioned why the promised financial reward had not been paid.
He also claimed that a road leading to the athlete’s residence had not been constructed despite an earlier announcement that Rs. 800,000 would be allocated for the project.
Premadasa further questioned reports suggesting that the government was considering revising the reward scheme to reduce the amount payable to successful athletes.
Responding, Sports Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage rejected the claim that an existing government circular entitled the athlete to Rs. 50 million.
He said an earlier reward arrangement had been approved by the Cabinet for a particular year, based on a recommendation from the Sports Council, and was not a permanent circular applicable to subsequent years.
The minister explained that the government had introduced a new arrangement with Cabinet approval to make payments for achievements in 2024 and 2025.
He said a fresh proposal had also been prepared to obtain Cabinet approval for payments relating to 2026.
The exchange became heated after the minister accused Premadasa of misleading Parliament, prompting the Opposition Leader to object to the allegation.

articles.title: Severe lightning warning: Red alerts issued for 19 districts
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued a severe lightning advisory for 25 districts across Sri Lanka today (21), with red alerts issued for 19 districts and amber alerts for six districts.
According to the advisory, thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several places in the Central, Sabaragamuwa, Northern, North-Central, North-Western, Eastern and Uva provinces.
The advisory, issued at 11.30 a.m. today (21), will remain valid until 1.30 a.m. tomorrow (22).
The Met Department warned that temporary localized strong winds may occur during thundershowers.
The public has been advised to take adequate precautions to minimise damage caused by lightning activity, including seeking shelter indoors, avoiding open areas and water bodies, and refraining from using wired telephones and connected electrical appliances during thunderstorms.
The Department also urged the public to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines and to contact local disaster management authorities for emergency assistance.

articles.title: Police investigate 14 over installation of Thileepan statue in Jaffna
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Police have recorded statements from 14 individuals, including politicians, in connection with the installation of a statue of former LTTE member Rasaiah Parthipan, also known as Thileepan, in Nallur, Jaffna.
Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala, speaking in Parliament today (21), said the statements were recorded from individuals allegedly involved in funding, constructing, promoting and organising the ceremony related to the statue.
The Minister said Police had launched an investigation into the incident and established that Thileepan was a member of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
He further stated that Police had taken the statue into custody and produced it before court as a case item.
According to Minister Wijepala, further legal action is being taken based on the advice of the Attorney General.
The remarks come in response to a question raised by Opposition MP Archchuna Ramanathan regarding the removal of the statue from the Thileepan Memorial Square in Jaffna on September 27, a day after commemorative events marking the 39th anniversary of Thileepan’s death concluded.
Previously, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa stated that Police had reported facts to the relevant court before removing the statue, noting that Sri Lankan law prohibits the promotion of banned organisations, including the LTTE.
Thileepan died in September 1987 following a hunger strike in Nallur, during which he presented several demands to the Indian government.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka Police have recorded statements from 14 individuals, including politicians, in connection with the installation of a statue of former LTTE member Rasaiah Parthipan, also known as Thileepan, in Nallur, Jaffna.

articles.title: Colombo Port Logistics Project cancelled over agreement concerns: Minister Bimal
articles.text:
Minister of Ports Bimal Rathnayake has revealed that concerns over the agreement to allocate 10 acres of land at the Colombo Port were among the reasons behind the government’s opposition to the proposed USD 280 million logistics project involving a Chinese company.
Speaking in Parliament, the Minister said the agreement involved allocating 10 acres of land located between the East and West Container Terminals at the Colombo Port to the logistics company.
He explained that while the government supported the proposed investment, it had concerns over the manner in which the agreement had been reached.
The Minister said he had personally worked to facilitate the project after assuming office, including bringing senior officials of the company to Sri Lanka for discussions.
“We held several discussions with company officials and made it clear that we supported the investment. However, we could not proceed under the existing agreement, as the proper procedures had not been followed,” he said.
Responding to allegations that the government’s actions had driven away investors, Minister Rathnayake rejected the claims, arguing that proceeding with investments under questionable agreements could discourage other potential investors.
His remarks come after the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) confirmed that the proposed USD 280 million logistics project at the Port of Colombo would not proceed.
The project was to be implemented through South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub (SACLH), a joint venture established in 2023 involving China Merchants Port Holdings Company Limited, which held a 70% stake, while the SLPA and Access Engineering PLC each held 15%.
According to the SLPA, the shareholders decided to discontinue the project following a review of external circumstances, commercial considerations and their respective interests.
The Authority also confirmed that approximately USD 29.8 million in equity contributions would be refunded to the shareholders in proportion to their stakes, subject to regulatory requirements and operational expenses.
Meanwhile, the SLPA has announced plans to develop an alternative logistics hub at the Colombo Port under a Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model, with investors to be selected through a competitive bidding process.
articles.summary: Minister of Ports Bimal Rathnayake has revealed that concerns over the agreement to allocate 10 acres of land at the Colombo Port were among the reasons behind the government’s opposition to the proposed USD 280 million logistics project involving a Chinese company.

articles.title: SC issues open warrant for arrest of Premalal Jayasekara
articles.text:
The Supreme Court today (21) issued an open warrant for the arrest of former State Minister Premalal Jayasekara after he failed to appear before court in connection with a case relating to a fatal shooting during the 2015 Presidential Election campaign.
The Supreme Court ordered that the warrant be issued through the Director of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and directed the Inspector General of Police (IGP) to take all necessary steps to ensure its prompt execution.
The Court also ordered that the two other defendants who appeared before court today be remanded in custody.
The case relates to a shooting incident at an election campaign rally held in Kahawatta in support of then-presidential candidate Maithripala Sirisena during the 2015 Presidential Election, which resulted in the death of an individual.
The Ratnapura High Court had previously sentenced Jayasekara and two other defendants to death after finding them guilty in connection with the incident.
However, the Court of Appeal subsequently overturned the convictions and ordered the acquittal and release of all three defendants.
An appeal was later filed before the Supreme Court by the aggrieved party challenging the Court of Appeal’s decision.
The Supreme Court concluded the hearing of the appeal on September 4 and issued notices directing all three defendants to appear before court today.
However, Jayasekara failed to appear, with Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara, appearing on behalf of the Attorney General, informing the Court that the former State Minister was overseas.
After considering the submissions, the three-judge Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena and Justices Achala Wengappuli and Gihan Kulatunga ordered the issuance of the open warrant.
articles.summary: The Supreme Court today (21) issued an open warrant for the arrest of former State Minister Premalal Jayasekara after he failed to appear before court in connection with a case relating to a fatal shooting during the 2015 Presidential Election campaign.

articles.title: Sri Lanka honours ‘Courageous Loser’ Olympian Ranatunge Karunananda
articles.text:
A special commemorative postage stamp has been issued in honour of renowned Sri Lankan athlete Ranatunge Karunananda, who gained international recognition for his determination and perseverance at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
The stamp was officially issued yesterday (20) at the Ministry of Mass Media, under the patronage of Minister of Health and Mass Media Nalinda Jayatissa, with the aim of preserving Sri Lanka’s sporting heritage and inspiring future generations.
Karunananda gained worldwide recognition during the 10,000-metre race at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, when he continued running until the finish despite all other competitors having completed the race.
His determination earned him the title “Courageous Loser,” making him a symbol of perseverance and sportsmanship.
Speaking at the event, Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said the commemorative stamp was not merely a tribute to an individual but also a recognition of the values of determination, discipline and mental strength demonstrated by Karunananda.
The Minister also highlighted that Karunananda’s inspiring story has been featured in Japanese school textbooks, reflecting the lasting impact of his achievements beyond Sri Lanka.
Born on May 21, 1936, in Kandy, Karunananda studied at Jinaraja College in Gampola and Ampitiya Maha Vidyalaya before representing the Sri Lanka Army Corps of Engineers in athletics at national and international levels.
The commemorative stamp issuance ceremony was attended by Deputy Minister of Mass Media Dr. Kaushalya Ariyarathne, Japanese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Akio Isomata, senior postal officials and members of Karunananda’s family.
articles.summary: A special commemorative postage stamp has been issued in honour of renowned Sri Lankan athlete Ranatunge Karunananda, who gained international recognition for his determination and perseverance at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

articles.title: Mireka Seascape Commences Main Building Construction, Appoints Sanken Constructions as Main Contractor
articles.text:
Mireka Seascape, a luxury coastal residential development by Overseas Realty (Ceylon) PLC, marked a significant milestone by celebrating the commencement of main building construction at a traditional groundbreaking ceremony held in Dodanduwa on 15 October 2026. This follows the successful completion of piling works and obtaining all government regulatory approvals, including approvals from the Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management Department and the Urban Development Authority (UDA).
As part of this milestone, Sanken Construction, a leading construction company in Sri Lanka, was appointed as the main contractor for the development. The appointment reflects Mireka Seascape’s commitment to maintaining high construction standards and delivering quality residential developments. “With Sanken Constructions’ extensive experience, expertise, and resources, the project is expected to be completed by November 2028, in line with the anticipated timeline and required highest quality standards,” a spokesperson for Mireka Seascape stated.
Launched in June 2025, Mireka Seascape comprises 168 luxury apartments and villas, offering
scenic views of the Indian Ocean and Rathgama Lake. The development combines contemporary residences with resort-style amenities, providing an appealing choice for those seeking a holiday home, a second residence, or a high-yield property investment. Strategically located in Dodanduwa, between Galle and Hikkaduwa, it offers a distinctive coastal lifestyle where residential comfort meets the appeal of a holiday destination.
Mireka Seascape features a range of amenities, including adult and children’s swimming pools, a fully equipped fitness centre, sauna and steam rooms, a yoga deck, bistro bar, sky lounge, viewing deck, multi-function room, children’s play areas, a work-from-home lounge, concierge services, and many other high-end amenities. The development also offers access to a beach suitable and safe for swimming, adding to its appeal as a coastal residential destination.
Building on the legacy of Overseas Realty (Ceylon) PLC’s landmark developments, including the World Trade Center Colombo and Havelock City Integrated Mixed-Use Development, Mireka Seascape reflects the company’s continued commitment to creating distinctive real estate developments defined by thoughtful planning, quality, and long-term value.
With main building construction now underway, Mireka Seascape moves closer to realizing its vision of becoming a distinctive coastal residential destination on Sri Lanka’s southern coastline.

With main building construction now underway, Mireka Seascape moves closer to realizing its vision of becoming a distinctive coastal residential destination on Sri Lanka’s southern coastline.

articles.title: Sri Lankan passenger’s missing cat found after week-long search at Dubai airport
articles.text:
A cat belonging to a Sri Lankan passenger that went missing at Dubai International Airport has been found after a week-long search.
The cat, named Chuuti, disappeared from its carrier on October 11 while being transported on a SriLankan Airlines flight from Dubai to Colombo.
According to an update from the SriLankan Airlines Dubai airport team, the cat was located inside a baggage carousel tunnel following an extensive search.
“After a week of tremendous effort by our DXB team, we successfully found the missing cat in the baggage carousel tunnel,” the update stated.

articles.title: “We will not allow cricket to collapse” – Sports Minister
articles.text:
Minister of Sports Sunil Kumara Gamage has assured that the government will not allow Sri Lanka Cricket to collapse, stating that legislative measures have already been initiated to develop the sport.
Speaking in Parliament today (21), the Minister said a new Bill aimed at reforming and developing cricket has already been presented to Parliament and is awaiting debate and approval.
“We will not allow the sport of Cricket to come to an end. Our government has already initiated the necessary process to develop the sport and achieve the results expected of it,” the Minister said.
He explained that the legislative process would take some time, but expressed confidence that the proposed reforms would help improve the standard of cricket in Sri Lanka.
The Minister also noted that previous governments had attempted similar reforms but faced challenges, while the current government was moving forward with the process with the support of the Opposition.
“Previous governments tried this and ministers were sent home. However, I, as the minister, am still here. The act has been presented to Parliament. The opposition is also assisting us. Let us work to fix the sport moving forward. We will not allow the sport of cricket to collapse,” he said.
The remarks were made in response to Opposition MP Hesha Withanage, who raised concerns over the deteriorating state of Sri Lanka Cricket.
MP Withanage claimed that the situation had worsened compared to the period under former Sri Lanka Cricket President Shammi Silva and questioned whether the government was taking new measures to revive the sport.

articles.title: FCEJ raises concerns over proposed Anti-Terrorism and Organised Crime Laws
articles.text:
The Feminist Collective for Economic Justice (FCEJ) has strongly criticized the National People’s Power (NPP) government over its proposed anti-terrorism and organised crime legislation, warning that the new laws could undermine fundamental rights, restrict public dissent and expand state powers.
In a statement issued on Tuesday (20), the collective accused the government of introducing oppressive legislation alongside economic policies that disproportionately affect low-income households, workers and vulnerable communities.
The FCEJ raised particular concerns over the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA) and Prevention of Organised Crime Bill, claiming that their provisions could allow broader policing powers, weaken judicial oversight and potentially criminalize legitimate protests and political opposition.
The collective also criticized the government’s economic policies, including austerity measures, privatization and foreign investment initiatives, claiming that these have increased financial hardships among ordinary citizens.
It further warned that the proposed NGO legislation and other recently introduced laws could restrict freedom of association, expression and public participation.
The FCEJ called on the NPP government to reconsider its legislative and economic agenda, accusing it of moving away from its electoral mandate to address exploitation and oppression.
Full statement below:
The Feminist Collective for Economic Justice (FCEJ) condemns the oppressive laws, particularly the most recent Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA) and the Organized Crime Bill, proposed by the government in October 2026. While addressing crime and terrorism, is a legitimate objective of a government, the unprecedented criminalization of poverty, expansion of broad policing power and the usurpation of the people’s judicial power are extremely concerning.
We believe that a closer look at the context reveals whose interests this legislative agenda serves. Authoritarianism fuelled by right wing fearmongering along the lines of terrorism, criminalizing migrants, minorities and the poor, and condemning countries of the global south as corrupt and indisciplined, is a global trend that protects wealth and wealth making. Similarly, economic policies that favour the wealthy have always required the strong police powers of the state to counter the dissent, disgruntlement, desperation and violence that are products of exploitation of labour and environment on the lives of ordinary people. It is clear that economic policies are driven by corporate greed in the form of a rapidly expanding export sector, mineral mining, land intensive green transitioning, financialization and privatization of essential public services.
The intensifying crisis upon the lives of the poor and working people of the country is all too visible. Economic insecurity of households prevails with continued low wages, increasing wage theft and increased cost of living. This has led to the expansion of household debt and exploitation of the working poor by predatory financial institutions. Precarious informal labour has expanded, increasing harassment and exploitation in the workplace. These stresses are compounded by the impact of climate change on access to water, agriculture and fishing livelihoods and on working conditions in plantations and factories, thus increasing economic burdens on families recovering from recurrent climate crises. There is widespread desperation to make ends meet, hold on to work, find multiple sources of income to feed one’s family, and thus the compulsion to migrate for work.
Anti-People Economic Policies
It is in the context of a growing frustration of ordinary people that the NPP government commits to expediting economic policies of privatization of essential services and continues to borrow foreign loans with conditionalities that work against its people. The NPP has continued austerity measures with removal of subsidies, low public spending and diminishing social security. It is pursuing private foreign investment without adequate protections for labour and environment as seen in the rush to implement large scale projects for mining, solar farms, wind power, palm oil plantations, and special economic zones. The corporate capture of the State is enabling bulldozing by an elite agenda that is pursuing wealth at the cost of people. It does so in the name of economic stability and fighting corruption. It is an economic trend driven by forces that are well aware of peoples’ hardship and desperation, and anticipates public protest and agitation. And so the ‘enemy’ is created and resisted by the State. It is the citizen protestor complaining of hardships and demanding the government steps down, the worker engaged in strike action that slows down production and the environmental activist who resists large scale projects by foreign investors, who are cast in the role of ‘enemy’. Anti people economic agendas have always been accompanied by oppressive laws.
Anti-People Laws
We are witnessing a rapid increase in the number of oppressive laws presented and passed under the NPP government In October 2026, we saw the government present the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA), which seeks to repeal and replace the Prevention of Terrorism Act of 1979. The Bill proposes a wider definition of ‘terrorism’ that potentially considers all forms of political opposition, rallies, protests and acts that ‘compel a government or international organization to do or abstain from doing any act’, as terrorism. The Bill proposes broad powers to the police, armed forces and coastguard, unprecedented power to the President in relation to proscribing organizations, unprecedented power to the Attorney General to settlements whereby prosecutions are deferred in return for public apologies or reparations, and restricts judicial supervision over arrests and detention. The PSTA lacks meaningful safeguards and access to justice for those against whom such laws have been arbitrarily or illegally used.
The Prevention of Organised Crime Bill introduces powers similar to those in the PSTA and additionally allows for confessions before police officers to be used in court. The confession clause is reminiscent of the same in the PTA that led to torture and cruel and degrading treatment of detainees to obtain confessions which were later used as the only evidence to convict and punish persons. Similarly the Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill applies to citizens and non-citizens who participate in offences which are, once again, so broadly defined, encapsulating acts which may be far removed from the core offence of ‘terrorism’.
The proposed NGO Bill demands mandatory registration of all voluntary social activities including of any groups of five or more working together, notification for any crowdfunding, imposes a duty on non governmental organizations to align with government policy, fines up to a maximum of one million rupees for administrative wrongdoings and lapses such as failing to provide information, and overall restricts freedom of association and expression.
In 2026 alone this government passed the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Act, The Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act and Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment) Act, creating legalised intrusion into privacy and State surveillance. The Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act of 2026 also dismantles community savings and fails to institute meaningful safeguards against exploitation of indebtedness, which in itself has significant socio-economic consequences. These laws are new legislative layers over an existing oppressive legislative landscape such as the Online Safety Act, the ICCPR Act, the Prevention of Terrorism Act and the Public Security Ordinance, and the plethora of colonial penal legislation that has been consistently deployed against a democratically and peacefully protesting public. The scheme and tone of all these laws is one of consolidating power, controlling people and expanding the power of officials to penalize citizen activity.
Listen to People and Change Course
In the two years the National People’s Power (NPP) has been in government after being elected with an overwhelming mandate for system change, we have witnessed the continuation of the oppressive laws and burdensome economic policies of Wickremesinghe’s two year stint. The NPP has opted for macroeconomic stability at the expense of increased precarity for the common people, especially working women who are shouldering the burden.
The pile up of all these oppressive laws accompanying economic policies that have and will continue to fail people is not a coincidence. It is chilling to watch the changing legislative landscape, without adequate explanation or justification and without any real consideration of public opinion or feedback.
We recall that it was in the late 1970s under the leadership of J R Jayawardene and the aggressive drive to liberalize the economy that development and deployment of a scheme of oppressive laws (Public Security Ordinance, Essential Services Act, Prevention of Terrorism Act) with similar intensity was last deployed.
We call out the anti-people project of the NPP government. You were voted in on a mandate to specifically reverse exploitation and oppression. You are failing to hear the ordinary people of Sri Lanka, you are failing to see the irreversible impact of the economic policies and police powers on the most vulnerable, you are promising those who support you a better life while building institutions of oppression that will work against their welfare, and your actions serve elite interests in the name of macro-economic stability and growth. Change course, it’s already too late.
The Feminist Collective for Economic Justice is a collective of feminist economists, scholars, feminist activists, university students and lawyers that came together in April 2022 to understand, analyze and give voice to policy recommendations based on lived realities in the current economic crisis in Sri Lanka.
articles.summary: The Feminist Collective for Economic Justice (FCEJ) has strongly criticized the National People’s Power (NPP) government over its proposed anti-terrorism and organised crime legislation, warning that the new laws could undermine fundamental rights, restrict public dissent and expand state powers.

articles.title: Sanath Jayasuriya-backed SPICEUP launches Ceylon cinnamon beverages, targets global markets
articles.text:
Samagi Spice Exports (Pvt) Ltd has recently launched SPICEUP, a new Sri Lankan beverage brand featuring cricket legend Sanath Jayasuriya as its brand ambassador, with plans to take value-added Ceylon cinnamon products to international markets.
The launch was held at the University of Ruhuna in Matara, marking the company’s expansion from traditional spice exports into the beverage industry.
The new beverage range, developed using Ceylon cinnamon and other locally grown spices, is promoted as a healthier alternative to conventional carbonated soft drinks, with reduced sugar content and an emphasis on natural spice extracts.
The SPICEUP range includes Original, Cream Soda, Power, GO, Cool, Burn, Memo+ and Zingy, available in cans and plastic bottles.
Samagi Spice Exports, a company with a history dating back to 1969, aims to transform Sri Lanka’s internationally recognised Ceylon cinnamon into value-added consumer products rather than relying primarily on raw spice exports.
As part of the launch, the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Ruhuna and Samagi Spice signed a preliminary non-disclosure agreement to support future research, product development and commercialisation.
The products were developed through research and collaboration involving the company’s research and development team and university researchers, with the aim of bringing innovative Sri Lankan beverages to the market.
The company plans to roll out SPICEUP islandwide within the next few months, while entering international markets remains a major objective.
Jayasuriya’s involvement as brand ambassador is expected to strengthen the brand’s visibility and support its efforts to promote Sri Lankan cinnamon-based beverages to a wider audience.
The company believes that developing finished consumer products using locally sourced cinnamon and spices could create new export opportunities while increasing the commercial value of Sri Lanka’s agricultural resources.
The launch brought together Samagi Spice Chairman Janaka Aberathna, Vice Chairman Janitha Aberathna, Professor Guththila Jayasinghe of the University of Ruhuna and other university and industry representatives.
Through SPICEUP, the company aims to establish a Sri Lankan beverage brand with international potential while promoting innovation, value addition and greater use of Ceylon cinnamon in finished consumer products.

Through SPICEUP, the company aims to establish a Sri Lankan beverage brand with international potential while promoting innovation, value addition and greater use of Ceylon cinnamon in finished consumer products.

articles.title: Sri Jayewardenepura University Leo Club Supports Habarana Families with ‘Pranadhara ’26’ Water Project

articles.text:
The Leo Club of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura has completed the second phase of its ‘Pranadhara ’26’ water security project , providing 10 water storage tanks to residents of Sewanagama in Habarana as part of an initiative to support families facing difficulties in accessing water.
The project was carried out in collaboration with the Lions Club of Godigamuwa Centennial , bringing together university youth leadership and community service to address an everyday challenge faced by residents in the area.
The donated tanks are intended to help households store water for drinking and other essential domestic needs, providing families with greater flexibility during periods when access to water is limited.
Water security remains an important issue for many rural communities in Sri Lanka’s Dry Zone. The United Nations Development Programme has previously highlighted the impact of prolonged droughts and climate variability on communities in the Dry Zone, including the importance of strengthening local water storage and community-managed drinking water infrastructure.
Against that background, ‘Pranadhara ’26’ focuses on a relatively simple but practical intervention helping families improve their ability to store water close to home.
The distribution programme was attended by a local council representative, the area’s Grama Niladhari and development officers, who joined Leo and Lions representatives in supporting the community initiative.
The University of Sri Jayewardenepura’s Leo Club has a longstanding relationship with the Lions Club of Godigamuwa Centennial. The university’s official website identifies the club as being sponsored by the Lions Club of Godigamuwa Centennial and says its purpose includes developing young leaders while encouraging service activities within communities.
That emphasis on youth-led community service is reflected in the latest phase of Pranadhara, where university students have moved beyond awareness-building to provide a practical resource directly to residents.
The initiative also highlights the value of smaller community projects in addressing local needs. While large-scale water supply infrastructure remains essential, household-level storage can offer additional support to families dealing with irregular access, particularly in areas vulnerable to dry conditions.
Sri Lanka continues to face wider challenges in extending safe and reliable drinking water to rural communities. In June 2026, the Government approved plans for a new small towns and rural water supply programme aimed at improving access to safe drinking water for around 60 families, reflecting the scale of the issue nationally.
For the Leo Club of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, however, ‘Pranadhara ’26’ demonstrates how young people can contribute at community level while developing leadership, social responsibility and an understanding of challenges beyond the university environment.
With its second phase now completed, the project has delivered a clear message alongside the water tanks themselves: meaningful community service does not always require a large intervention — sometimes, meeting a basic need in the right place can make an immediate difference to everyday life.
articles.summary: The Leo Club of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura has completed the second phase of its ‘Pranadhara ’26’ water security project , providing 10 water storage tanks to residents of Sewanagama in Habarana as part of an initiative to support families facing difficulties in accessing water.

articles.title: Hackers demanded USD 50,000 after breaching SriLankan Airlines systems, Dayasiri alleges
articles.text:
Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekara has alleged that hackers who compromised SriLankan Airlines’ computer systems demanded a ransom of USD 50,000 in cryptocurrency, warning that the national carrier remains vulnerable to further cyberattacks.
Addressing Parliament on Tuesday (20), Jayasekara claimed that SriLankan Airlines’ systems were compromised in June 2026, with hackers subsequently claiming responsibility for the attack on the dark web.
He alleged that the attackers had released a video claiming to have gained control of the airline’s systems and demanded USD 50,000 in cryptocurrency.
“The entire SriLankan Airlines system was hijacked. They even released a video claiming responsibility,” Jayasekara told Parliament.
The MP claimed that the airline’s email systems had also been compromised, raising serious concerns about the security of its digital infrastructure.
He further alleged that the airline’s email protection system had experienced problems following the attack.
Jayasekara warned that the alleged cyberattack could have serious consequences for the national carrier’s operations.
“Even now, the system is in the hands of hackers. They could bring it down at any time,” he claimed.
The opposition MP also raised questions about previous financial irregularities involving SriLankan Airlines, referring to payments made through accounts in Dubai and India.
He questioned whether the incidents were connected to weaknesses in the airline’s cybersecurity systems.
Jayasekara alleged that efforts to investigate the incident had been obstructed, claiming that an official who attempted to pursue an investigation was subsequently subjected to an inquiry initiated through the Presidential Secretariat.
He also claimed that assistance had been offered by the United States through representatives in Singapore to address the cybersecurity vulnerabilities, but that the government had not yet accepted the offer.
The MP urged the government to immediately investigate the alleged breach, secure the airline’s digital infrastructure and explain what action had been taken to prevent further attacks.

articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to present the Import and Export (Control) Regulations No. 08 of 2026 to Parliament, enforcing mandatory Sri Lanka Standards (SLS) testing compliance for imported passenger car tyres and pneumatic tyres for three-wheelers.
The proposal was submitted by the President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development, based on recommendations from the Ministry of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development. The new measures aim to establish a fair competitive landscape for domestic tire manufacturers while safeguarding consumer safety and quality assurance.
Enacted via Extraordinary Gazette Notification No. 2508/27 on October 1, 2026, the updated regulations amend existing standardization protocols. Under the new rules, imported passenger car tyres under HS Code 4011.10.90 must comply with Sri Lanka Standard 1212, while pneumatic tyres for three-wheeled vehicles under HS Code 4011.90.10 must adhere to Sri Lanka Standard 1347.

articles.title: Tattoos, arrests and detention: Saliya Pieris challenges Justice Minister’s explanation
articles.text:
Former Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President and President’s Counsel Saliya Pieris has challenged Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara’s explanation of the proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that its broad provisions and lack of safeguards could expose ordinary citizens to arbitrary arrests and prolonged detention.
Responding to the minister’s statement in Parliament on Tuesday (20), Pieris questioned who would determine whether a person’s tattoos or clothing resembled those associated with organized criminal groups.
“Who decides at the point of arrest whether the tattoo or clothes are similar to those used by criminal groups?” Pieris asked.
He said such decisions would initially be made by police officers who would be vested with extensive powers under the proposed legislation.
Earlier, Justice Minister Nanayakkara rejected claims that individuals could be arrested simply for having tattoos, long hair or certain clothing styles. He explained that the relevant provisions applied to characteristics associated with known members of organized criminal groups and did not criminalize personal appearance.
However, Pieris argued that the minister’s explanation failed to address the wider implications of the proposed law.
According to Pieris, the bill would permit detention orders to be issued by the relevant ministry secretary at the request of a Deputy Inspector General of Police or the Inspector General of Police, allowing suspects to be detained for up to two months without judicial authorization and potentially for up to one year thereafter.
He further claimed that even without a detention order, a magistrate would have no option but to remand a person produced under the proposed law, regardless of whether sufficient supporting material had been presented.
“If the police say the tattoo or clothing concerned is that of an organised criminal group and produces the person under this law the Magistrate will have to remand,” he said.
Pieris also raised concerns that suspects would have to seek bail from the High Court, creating additional difficulties for ordinary citizens.
He criticized provisions allowing police-recorded confessions to be admitted as evidence in court, warning that such measures could encourage torture and abuse.
The former BASL president recalled that many members of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna had experienced torture, abuse and prolonged detention under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) and Emergency Regulations.
He warned that laws including the PTA, Emergency Regulations and ICCPR Act had been misused under successive governments, causing considerable suffering.
Pieris also questioned the drafting process, saying that, to his knowledge, the bill had not been prepared by the Justice Ministry and had not undergone a public consultation process.
“Those who are trying to justify this new Bill as being a necessity, must recall how the PTA, the Emergency Regulations, the ICCPR Act and other laws have been abused under successive governments and the untold suffering and harm it has caused to people,” he said.
Pieris concluded by warning that those who had witnessed the misuse of such legislation and its consequences for victims could recognize the dangers posed by the new bill.
The proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill was presented to Parliament for its first reading on October 20 and has not yet become law.
The Justice Minister, meanwhile, maintained that the provision concerning clothing, hand signals and tattoos was modeled on Singapore’s organized crime legislation and was intended to help identify membership in criminal organizations rather than criminalize ordinary citizens’ appearance.
articles.summary: Former Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President and President’s Counsel Saliya Pieris has challenged Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara’s explanation of the proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, warning that its broad provisions and lack of safeguards could expose ordinary citizens to arbitrary arrests and prolonged detention.

articles.title: Cabinet approves Rs. 15.07 Bn revised plan to complete Kolonnawa flood control project
articles.text:
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a revised three-year plan valued at Rs. 15,077.82 million (Rs. 15.07Bn) to resume and complete the remaining work on the Kolonnawa Stormwater Drainage and Environment Improvement Project.
Originally launched in 2019, the project experienced severe delays due to the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent economic recession. To address these setbacks, the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development submitted a newly restructured plan and updated cost framework to the Cabinet.
The newly approved strategy focuses on several major infrastructure tasks, including completing the 3,250 meter Salalihini Mawatha canal and constructing the 3,868 meter Dahamwala canal. It also involves creating dedicated water retention ponds and water storage areas to manage heavy rainfall effectively.
Additionally, workers will repair the 4,475 meter Passiyana canal and the 650 meter Dandukotuwa canal, restore the Dandutota flood gate and deploy three mobile pumps, each capable of pumping stormwater at a rate of one cubic meter per second. To ensure fair treatment for residents, an estimated Rs. 1,015 million has been allocated under a specialized relief package to compensate affected families for necessary land acquisitions and potential disruptions to their livelihoods during execution.

articles.title: Kavanthissa’s Death: Govt. says multiple investigations underway
articles.text:
The government is treating the death of Kavanthissa, the tusker fatally injured in a shooting, with due concern, Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said.
Responding to questions from journalists about the handling of the elephant’s treatment by the Department of Wildlife Conservation, Jayatissa said investigations were underway to determine whether there had been delays, lapses or negligence in its treatment, as well as to identify those responsible for the shooting.
“I believe we should not challenge the knowledge of the veterinarians who were involved in this,” he said, adding that the veterinarians had made considerable efforts, as stated by the subject minister in Parliament earlier today.
Jayatissa said the investigations were aimed not only at identifying those responsible but also at preventing similar incidents in the future.
The post-mortem examination is being conducted by the veterinary department of the University of Peradeniya, which is expected to submit its findings to court, he said.
An internal inquiry is also underway, involving a committee comprising three members: the director of the National Zoological Department, the investigations director of the Ministry of Environment and a senior lecturer at the University of Peradeniya’s Faculty of Veterinary Medicine.
Separately, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed a six-member panel of experts led by former ministry secretary Sarath Wijesinghe. The panel includes Prof. Saminda Fernando, Prof. Anil Pushpakumara, Prof. Kalinga Padmalal, Dr. Jagath Gunawardana and Attorney-at-Law Charaka Jayaratne.
The Criminal Investigation Department is also conducting a separate investigation, Jayatissa said.
Two suspects arrested in connection with the shooting have been remanded until Oct. 28. According to Jayatissa, the arrests followed information provided by members of the public to the Western Province Range Forest Office, after which the Walana Anti-Corruption Unit acted on the information.
Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the first suspect, while further items were recovered from another suspect based on information provided during the investigation, he said.
Jayatissa clarified that four other individuals arrested by the Walana Anti-Corruption Unit were not taken into custody in connection with the elephant’s death. Investigations remain ongoing.
He also acknowledged staff shortages at the Department of Wildlife Conservation, saying it had only 17 veterinarians, of whom 14 were serving in the field. The department hopes to recruit additional veterinarians, he added.
articles.summary: The government is treating the death of Kavanthissa, the tusker fatally injured in a shooting, with due concern, Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said.

articles.title: Rocell Starlight®, Setting a New Standard in Polished Ceramics
articles.text:
Celestial brilliance, crystalline depth: Rocell’s latest surface innovation transforms the way polished ceramic tiles interact with light.
For the first time in Sri Lanka, Rocell introduces ‘Starlight’, an advanced surface innovation that brings crystal-like depth and brilliance to polished porcelain tiles. Inspired by the brilliance of the cosmos, Rocell Starlight captures the depth, radiance, and natural interplay of light found among the stars. As light moves across the tile, subtle variations in reflection create a captivating sense of depth and movement, transforming the surface from a flat polished finish into something that feels almost celestial. Building on Rocell’s commitment to design, quality, and innovation, Rocell Starlight represents a new chapter in ceramic surface development.
Unlike conventional polished tiles, which create a largely uniform reflection, Starlight technology introduces greater depth and visual complexity through a specialised polishing process. Crystal-like formations emerge from within the ceramic surface, creating a distinctive interaction with light. The result is a refined finish with greater depth, contrast, and visual presence.
What sets the technology apart is that the effect is not printed onto the tile or added as a decorative layer. A specialised granulate is incorporated into the manufacturing process before polishing, allowing the crystalline effect to emerge from within the surface itself. This gives each tile a rich, authentic character while maintaining the consistency required for modern residential and commercial applications.
Designed for homeowners, renovators, architects, and interior designers, the technology offers a sophisticated new material for floors, feature walls, and statement interiors.
With Starlight, Rocell continues to bring global surface innovation to the Sri Lankan market while advancing the possibilities of ceramic design. More than a new finish, it reflects Rocell’s ongoing pursuit of bringing the world’s finest designs and design technologies to Sri Lanka and to its discerning customers.

Jayatissa expressed hope that the power plant would return to normal operations from tomorrow, in line with assurances given by the authorities.

articles.text:

articles.title: Namal questions proposed organized crime law, warns of return to 1988–89 era
articles.text:
Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer and opposition MP Namal Rajapaksa has raised concerns over the proposed Organized Crime Prevention Bill, warning that it could pave the way for repressive practices similar to those seen during the 1988–89 period.
Rajapaksa made the remarks in Parliament on Tuesday (20), after arriving from remand custody to attend parliamentary proceedings.
“Do you need a new law to arrest someone who has a tattoo displaying the symbol of an organized criminal gang?” he questioned.
Rajapaksa accused the government of attempting to introduce repressive measures under the pretext of combating organized crime.
Referring to explanations provided by the justice minister regarding tattoos associated with criminal groups, Rajapaksa questioned whether the proposed legislation could result in individuals being targeted based on their physical appearance.
He recalled earlier practices involving individuals identified as Island Reconvicted Criminals (IRCs), claiming that people had been targeted over their hairstyles and beards.
Rajapaksa drew parallels with the 1988–89 period, alleging that the government was attempting to revive similar practices through legislation.
He also questioned the government’s priorities, pointing to continuing shootings and killings linked to organized crime while accusing authorities of failing to address the economic difficulties faced by the public.
Rajapaksa urged the government to focus on unemployment, the rising cost of living and other pressing public concerns rather than introducing legislation that he claimed could be used for repression.
The proposed legislation was presented to Parliament for its first reading on October 20.

articles.title: Can you be jailed for having tattoos? Justice Minister issues clarification
articles.text:
Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara has rejected claims that Sri Lanka’s proposed Organized Crime Prevention Bill would allow individuals to be arrested simply for having tattoos, long hair or particular clothing styles.
Addressing Parliament on Tuesday (20), the minister said misleading interpretations of the proposed legislation were circulating on social media, creating unnecessary fear among the public.
The bill was presented to Parliament for its first reading, with the government seeking to introduce new legal provisions to investigate, prosecute and prevent crimes committed by organized criminal groups.
Nanayakkara said some individuals were falsely claiming that people could be imprisoned for having tattoos or adopting certain hairstyles.
“Wearing clothes of your choice, getting a tattoo or having a hairstyle you prefer are fundamental rights,” the minister said.
Explaining Section 4(2) of the proposed legislation, Nanayakkara said it outlines 12 factors that may be considered when determining whether an individual belongs to an organized criminal group.
One factor refers to clothing styles, hand signals, language or tattoos commonly used by known members of organized criminal organizations.
However, he stressed that these were not independent criminal offenses and that the provision concerned suspected membership in organized criminal groups rather than the appearance of ordinary individuals.
The minister described the provision as a “rebuttable presumption,” explaining that it does not constitute conclusive evidence of criminal involvement.
He said similar indicators are used internationally by investigators to identify gang membership, citing practices in countries including Japan, the United States, Australia and Singapore.
Nanayakkara also said the proposed legislation was intended to strengthen law enforcement against organized crime, drug trafficking, murders, abductions and other serious offenses.
He maintained that existing legislation was insufficient to effectively investigate and prosecute certain activities linked to organized criminal networks.
He welcomed criticism of the bill and said the government was prepared to consider suggestions during parliamentary discussions.
Nanayakkara also encouraged those who believed the legislation violated constitutional rights to challenge it before the Supreme Court.
He accused certain political groups and social media commentators of deliberately misrepresenting the proposed law for political purposes.
The minister reiterated that individuals would not face criminal charges merely for having tattoos, growing their hair or wearing particular clothing.
The bill remains at the first-reading stage in Parliament.
Meanwhile, legal experts have raised separate concerns about provisions relating to police-recorded confessions and restrictions on bail under the proposed legislation.
articles.summary: Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara has rejected claims that Sri Lanka’s proposed Organized Crime Prevention Bill would allow individuals to be arrested simply for having tattoos, long hair or particular clothing styles. The minister reiterated that individuals would not face criminal charges merely for having tattoos, growing their hair or wearing particular clothing.
